transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well... I guess I'm just having trouble getting things done. I can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's important. 

I do computer support, and... well, I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I realize I've reread the same log entries three times. And I still don't know what they actually say. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention and focus when you were a child in school?

Yeah... I guess so. My mother actually still jokes about my old grade school report cards. She says they always wrote that I was bright, but... well, that I never stayed in my seat. Or I'd just blurt out answers. And I guess I lost my homework a lot... even when I actually did it. So... yeah.
Nowadays, do you still find yourself feeling restless or having difficulty sitting still for long periods?

Yeah. I guess I do. Um... even when I'm supposed to just sit still and listen, it's... I don't know. It just feels like there's a motor humming under my skin. Like I need to stand up, or check something... or just move to the next problem right that second. So... yes.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or finishing their sentences before they have a chance to finish speaking?

I guess... yeah. I do. Mostly at work. When someone is explaining a tech issue, the answer just sort of... jumps into my head. 

I know I shouldn't, but I end up cutting them off. Or talking over them. Sometimes I just reach over and grab their keyboard before they even finish explaining what's wrong. So... yes.
Do these difficulties with focus and restlessness also cause problems in your life outside of work, such as at home or in your personal relationships?

I guess... yeah. It does. Um... things have been a bit strained at home. Mostly about money. 

Since I lost the... the structure of my old job, my reputation has taken a pretty big hit. I've, uh, lost some freelance clients. Even missed out on a senior service-manager role. And... well, my wife and I have to worry about the finances now, because... I don't know. People just don't trust me to follow through on things anymore. So... yeah. It affects things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity dating back to childhood (grade school report cards noting difficulty staying seated, blurting out answers, and losing homework) and persisting into adulthood. Current symptoms include sustained attention deficits, internal restlessness/motor agitation, and conversational/behavioral impulsivity. These symptoms have been continuously elevated for approximately 22 months and cause pervasive functional impairment across occupational, financial, and relational domains, fulfilling criteria for Disturbance of activity and attention (ADHD).
